answer: Divergent history attestation. Each agent keeps a signed append-only log with a monotonically increasing counter, and peers refuse work from any identity whose log fails a consistency check against earlier copies they hold. A clone starting from copied state cannot forge divergent past entries without breaking signatures, so all clones collapse into one detectable lineage; an attacker must run each identity from genesis, paying full compute and copper costs per log, and cannot reuse dune-learned context across them.
